#### What this PR does / why we need it:
This PR fixes caliculation of pod termination grace period.
Now, when execute `kubectl delete pod --force --grace-period=0`, "pod "nginx" force deleted" message is shown and the result of `kubectl get pod nginx` is `Error from server (NotFound): pods "nginx" not found`. So pod seems deleted.
But actually, pod process is still living because `terminationGracePeriodSeconds` is priored than `--force --grace-period=0`.
This behavior has been changed sometime. In ver1.18, `--force --grace-period=0` behavior was correct.
please see #120449 .
This PR fixes caliculation of pod termination grace period.
By this change, when execute `kubectl delete pod --force --grace-period=0`, pod process also killed immediately.

Currently, the tests being fixed here shows the change of grace period to `1`.

> @tuibeovince Thank you for your comment.
> 
> > can you explain the logic why you move the TerminationGracePeriodSeconds before the DeletionGracePeriodSeconds?
> 
> The reason is: originally, when I execute `kubectl delete pod --force --grace-peropd=0`, pod wasn't deleted immedeately. Because `pod.Spec.TerminationGracePeriodSeconds` has priority over `pod.DeletionGracePeriodSeconds` which means the value of `--grace-period` option. This behavior is different from what users expect. user expect that the value of `--grace-period` option override the `pod.Spec.TerminationGracePeriodSeconds` as written in the [docs](https://kubernetes.io/docs/concepts/workloads/pods/pod-lifecycle/#pod-termination-forced). In order to make behave like we expect, below block must be put at first in the calculateEffectiveGracePeriod() function, I think.
> 
> ```
> pod.Spec.TerminationGracePeriodSeconds; override != nil {
> 		if *override < gracePeriod {
> 			gracePeriod = *override
> 		}
> 	}
> ```

Thank you for your explanation. I think this makes a lot of sense. But I just hope we can make it more understandable in the comments within the source eventually. Also, maybe hear another person's opinion about this too.

@YuikoTakada  Thank you for your PR! This is an important fix, but it needs to be carefully tested, considering importance of this area and a lot of other changes in it. It would be nice to spot when regression was introduced and why. Adding e2e test case would be nice too.

Will review. 

It’s important to note that even when pods are force deleted via the API, the kubelet will still send SIGTERM and wait a minimal time (1-2s) before sending SIGKILL.  This is by design and has been since the introduction of graceful delete.

It looks like from the results of the node e2e that this indeed broke static pods.

A fix for the problem described (API pod force delete while running followed by CREATE when we don’t observe the force delete) may have to be specific to API pods, and exclude static pods.  Ideally that logic would be brought as close as possible to the config loop (in SyncKnownPods).

I will review the changes in calculateEffectiveGracePeriod - I would expect an override to “win” over the meta deletionperiodinseconds, so that could be a separate bug.

To ensure we don’t regress in the future, we really need a node e2e test added that recreates the issue described (including the problematic behavior) before accepting a fix.  Unit tests aren’t sufficient, but fortunately it sounds like you have a consistent reproduction?

For the node e2e test, it would be creating a pod that uses its full grace period (we have test images that can do that), force deleting it, then immediately recreating the pod with the same name.  The new pod should start within a few seconds, and not have to wait out the grace period.

issue_context.title: "kubectl delete pod" doesn't kill pod's process immediately when specifying --grace-period=0
issue_context.body:
### What happened?

As far as we read the help of "kubectl delete", it looks like that --grace-period=0 immediately kills Pod's processes.
```
    --force=false:
        If true, immediately remove resources from API and bypass graceful deletion. Note that immediate deletion of
        some resources may result in inconsistency or data loss and requires confirmation.

    --grace-period=-1:
        Period of time in seconds given to the resource to terminate gracefully. Ignored if negative. Set to 1 for
        immediate shutdown. Can only be set to 0 when --force is true (force deletion).
```

In fact, processes gets killed if we set --grace-period=0 in ver1.18.
But it seems that the behehavior got changed between ver1.18 and ver1.27.

- ver1.18 ... grace-period=0 killes Pod's processes immediately
- ver1.27 ... grace-period=0 sends SIGTERM to Pod's processes first, then wait for Pod's terminationGracePeriodSeconds before sending SIGKILL. As a result, when I execute `kubectl delete pod grace-period=0 --force` , message "pod pod-name force deleted" is shown, but pod's process is not killed immediately. It lives during `terminationGracePeriodSeconds` .



### What did you expect to happen?

when execute "kubectl delete pod --force --grace-period=0" , process will have been deleted immediately unless wating during `terminationGracePeriodSeconds`

### How can we reproduce it (as minimally and precisely as possible)?

nginx-pod.yaml:
```
apiVersion: v1
kind: Pod
metadata:
  name: nginx
spec:
  terminationGracePeriodSeconds: 300
  containers:
  - name: nginx
    image: nginx:1.14.2
    command: [ 'sleep', '12345']
    ports:
    - containerPort: 80
```

```

@SergeyKanzhelev Thank you. I'll test with v1.28.
Just for supplementary information; the grace period recalculation started in v1.22. Since then, the logic for changing the grace period values weren't changed until 1.28 (current released version).
is there any workaround for this?
No, There is no workaround currently.

The intended behavior here is that when the kubelet observes a pod has been force deleted, that it sends a SIGTERM to container processes as soon as it can, and then should force stop the processes with SIGKILL within 2s to give the pod an opportunity to shutdown cleanly.

Because a force deletion is the removal of a pod without waiting for clean shutdown, the kubelet handles that termination as part of its exceptional cleanup loop, which might take an extra few seconds to react.

The kubelet must never stop a container immediately with SIGKILL, and may only send that signal after attempting a SIGTERM.

EDIT: It is definitely a bug when the kubelet waits for a full termination grace period on force delete (vs the minimal wait), it’s just not immeditate in any scenario.  The bug here is waiting for the full grace period, not the fact that SIGTERM is sent.

@smarterclayton Thank you for your comments. In latest version, `SIGTERM` is sent immediately when `kubectl delete pod --force --grace-period=0` is executed. Because when execute `kubectl get pods` immediately after `kubectl delete pod --force --grace-period=0` , `No resources found in default namespace.` message is shown. But process is still living during `terminationGracePeriodSeconds` (default: 300). 
This behavior is different from ideal behavior that  you said " it sends a SIGTERM to container processes as soon as it can, and then should force stop the processes with SIGKILL within 2s"

review_comments: Can you explain why you are making this change?  Spec is not the most correct value, it is overridden by the value in metadata?

If `gracePeriod == 0 || ` is still existing, when I execute `kubectl delete pod --force --grace-period=0`, then return value of calculateEffectiveGracePeriod() become `pod.Spec.TerminationGracePeriodSeconds` (default: 300) because `gracePeriod` value is 0 and go through this(L.986) if statement.

The described behavior change in the test looks correct - if we observe a CREATE
while the pod is still terminating, we should be indicating to the CRI that the pod definition has been force deleted but without us observing it.  However, the test coverage here seems inadequate to convince me other scenarios might not be broken.

In particular, static pods may depend on the described behavior (because static pods can use a UID that doesn’t change on restart, but still need graceful termination).  It might be that we have to adapt this fix to differentiate between those two scenarios, and ensure static pod behavior is preserved.
Thank you for your comments. I'll look into static pod behavior.
This is incorrect, we must never allow a grace period of zero to be sent to CRI.

This was done in version 1.19. After version 1.23, it is not allowed to send a zero grace period to the CRI.
